title: The InviTE Corpus: Annotating Invectives in Tudor English Texts for Computational Modeling
benchmark_measurement: Detection of invective language, particularly religious invectives (e.g., targeting sinful behavior, political-religious misconduct, religious belief, or confession), in Early Modern English texts from the Protestant Reformation era.
findings: Fine-tuned models, particularly MacBERTh which was pre-trained on historical data, significantly outperform larger general-purpose LLMs (Llama 3, Qwen 2) in a zero-shot setting for the task of detecting invective language in historical religious texts. This highlights the importance of domain-specific pre-training and task-specific fine-tuning for specialized historical analysis.
